propositions: The snapshot janitor's absolute 2-GiB free-space watermark is disk-size-blind and unreachable on a 30-GiB root volume, only crossing at 93.3% used — above the 85% alarm floor and above the 90% peak reached in the incident.

Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree on a ref that advances every 26 seconds, accumulating at 4.4 GiB/h on the container's writable layer because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset.

The snapshot store sits on the container's writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is set nowhere in docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile.reviewbot, or fetch-secrets.sh, so store_root() falls through to tempfile.gettempdir().
The 7-day cold-trim trigger is dead code because the container lifetime is hours (23 recreations in 4 days), so no entry can reach 7 days old.
The byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 and the janitor module docstring is absent from _gc_pass; only the free-space and age triggers exist.

Adding a volume-relative free_watermark_pct term (as max of absolute 2-GiB floor and percentage of total disk) with hysteresis to a target margin allows reclaim to engage before the 85% alarm floor on small volumes.
